description: We are Earth Second Moon team, passionate about Remote Sensing, GIS, climate change, and Earth observation. Our NASA Space Apps project focuses on developing an application to monitor climate change trends using satellite data. We welcome members skilled in Remote Sensing, GIS, Google Earth Engine, AI/ML, data science, web/mobile development, and visualization. Join us to turn space data into real-world climate insights!
summary:
Our project, Earth System Trend Detective website, is an interactive, automated, and regularly updated global environmental monitoring platform designed to detect, analyze, and visualize significant changes across interconnected Earth systems.

We developed six interactive, automated, and continuously updated dashboards in 1)global agriculture monitoring , 2)global water bodies monitoring , 3)global water cycle monitoring , 4)global carbon sequestration monitoring ,5)global day and night LST monitoring , 6)global air pollution monitoring, enabling users to explore environmental variables, investigate regional changes, visualize historical trends, and assess their statistical significance. The platform is supported by 24 real-world environmental case studies, covering phenomena such as European drought, East African locust invasion, Lake Mead depletion, UAE flash flooding, Amazon productivity, and the Pacific Northwest heat dome.

Our integrated workflow combines satellite data acquisition, regional analysis, time-series visualization, and statistical significance testing using multiple statistical methods to distinguish meaningful environmental trends from random fluctuations like P-value significance 

By transforming complex Earth science data into accessible, interactive insights, our solution empowers students, researchers, and decision-makers to understand environmental changes, identify emerging risks, and support evidence-based decisions for a more sustainable future.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective Website is an integrated, interactive, automated, and continuously updated global environmental monitoring platform that transforms satellite-derived Earth observation data into meaningful information about changes and trends across interconnected Earth systems.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

We developed six interactive, automated, and continuously updated global monitoring dashboards, each dedicated to a major Earth system component:

  1. Global Agriculture Monitoring: Detecting changes in vegetation conditions, agricultural productivity, and vegetation trends.
  2. Global Water Bodies Monitoring: Monitoring changes in the extent and distribution of lakes, reservoirs, and other surface water bodies.
  3. Global Water Cycle Monitoring: Investigating changes in water-cycle variables and their interconnected environmental patterns.
  4. Global Carbon Sequestration Monitoring: Tracking changes in carbon-related indicators and ecosystem productivity.
  5. Global Day and Night Land Surface Temperature (LST) Monitoring: Analyzing global temperature patterns and long-term thermal changes during daytime and nighttime.
  6. Global Air Pollution Monitoring: Investigating changes in atmospheric pollution indicators and their spatial and temporal trends.

Each dashboard follows an integrated workflow:

Variable Selection → Satellite Data Acquisition → Regional Analysis → Time-Series Visualization → Statistical Significance Testing.

Users can investigate environmental variables, explore historical trends, compare different geographical regions, and determine whether observed changes are statistically significant.

2. Global Environmental Case Studies

To demonstrate the platform's practical capabilities, we incorporated 24 real-world environmental case studies (four per dashboard). These include European drought, East African locust invasion, Lake Mead water depletion, UAE flash flooding, Amazon ecosystem productivity, and the Pacific Northwest heat dome.

The platform also demonstrates statistical evidence through p-value analysis, t-tests, Wilcoxon tests, Mann–Whitney tests, permutation tests, and autocorrelation-adjusted statistical testing.

Examples of investigated findings include:

  • 70% decline in East African Leaf Area Index (LAI).
  • Significant contraction of Lake Urmia's water area.
  • A temperature increase of +12.5°C during the Pacific Northwest heat dome.
  • Significant rising Net Primary Productivity (NPP) trends in Australia and Europe.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes complex Earth science information accessible through interactive visualizations and scientific evidence. Its intended impact includes:

  • Helping researchers identify and investigate significant environmental trends.
  • Supporting decision-makers with evidence-based environmental information.
  • Raising public awareness of global environmental changes.
  • Enabling students to explore real-world Earth system phenomena.
  • Improving understanding of the interconnected nature of Earth's environmental systems.

Ultimately, the platform aims to transform environmental monitoring from simply observing changes into understanding their direction, magnitude, geographical distribution, and statistical significance.

4. Tools and Technologies

The solution is based on cloud computing of google cloud satellite-derived Earth observation data of NASA and its partners , automated data acquisition and processing, interactive dashboard development, time-series analysis, and statistical testing.

The specific programming languages are JavaScript , HTML , CSS .

5. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation is bringing six major Earth system monitoring components together within one integrated global trend-detection concept.

Rather than presenting satellite maps as isolated observations, our platform connects spatial analysis, historical time series, regional case studies, and statistical significance testing. This allows users to investigate not only whether an environmental variable is increasing or decreasing, but also whether the observed trend is statistically meaningful.

We also considered global accessibility, automated updates, scientific reliability, ease of interpretation, and the needs of different audiences, including students, researchers, and decision-makers.

Our vision is to make everyone an Earth System Trend Detective website, capable of discovering, investigating, and understanding the changes shaping our planet.
